fresh_front_and_interface_checks.check: The connected compact ambient manifold and its dimension precede the background and potential notation in the Introduction.
Non-Kahler ambient geometry is distinguished from a nonclosed smooth background.
Constant bounded-potential mass for a closed background is distinguished from non-pluripolar mass lost at singularities.
The mixed-form mass-variation criterion uses powers1 through n-1 and is vacuous on a curve.
The standard Hopf threefold has positive lower mass and infinite upper mass; the separate balanced example has finite upper mass and zero lower mass.
The raw primitive obstruction requires dimension at least two and a local C2 neighbourhood; the curve exception is preserved.
The Gauduchon trace conserves its stated linear quantity for arbitrary smooth theta; the fixed positive volume and mean-zero normalization are specified.
Weak Gauduchon trace convergence agrees with normalized L1 convergence without implying nonlinear Monge-Ampere control.
Damping can make an infinite measure finite; removal of damping requires the stated uniform tail control.
For smooth positive density the normalization scalar is an unknown; adjoint and variational formulas retain their dependence on the potential.
The Lp individual-density equation assumes p>1 and a nonzero nonnegative density; it separates scalar uniqueness from potential selection.
Potential uniqueness for degeneracy retains the additional smooth-data and connected dense positivity-locus assumptions.
The divisorial normalization functional does not recover an entire singularity type.
Bounded-difference ordinary types are distinct from all-weight multiplier-ideal types; the positive-mass Kahler qualification for I-goodness is retained.
Analytic dyadic approximation includes its curvature correction on a fixed Hermitian background, and ordinary topology can fail separation.
Smooth gauge transport changes the zero obstacle; the all-obstacle formulation has the stated covariance.
The higher-dimensional all-obstacle equivalence retains smooth big BMP and positive lower ideal-volume hypotheses; curves and product loci have separate results.
Type volumes are infima or suprema over the declared representatives, rather than the mass of one chosen potential.
Positive-lower-volume model completeness is a metrization statement; zero-volume nonseparation, complete polar variation on curves and restricted product loci remain distinct.
The two general finite-measure regimes retain respectively their smaller-background reference and BMP big-background positive-lower-reference-volume assumptions.
Relative-envelope membership is not silently replaced by bounded ordinary difference; prescribed poles distinguish residual positivity from forced minimal divisors and descent.
The finite analytic-boundary distance theorem retains Holder potential, smooth strict positivity off a proper nonempty analytic boundary and the required metric hypotheses.
A restriction identically minus infinity can still carry ideal trace data; compatible trace realization remains a separate problem.
Section-counting uses closed line-bundle curvature; Gauduchon degrees and partial-kernel fibration results retain their separate hypotheses.
The Introduction route matches all33 ordered chapters and10 parts, keeps the excluded Nakamaye source excluded, and places the additional mass assumptions in PartIX.
Conventions retain ddc log normalization and the absence of an implicit1/n! factor; all formal questions and their catalogue locations match the final body.
